events.name: Creative Edge
events.description:
THE CREATIVE EDGE
Forming a creative minority.

The paradox of a mature faith is that you become more engaged in the world by being less formed by it.
We live in a world that is constantly asking us to produce, perform, build, and become more. And for those of us who follow Jesus, there is a deeper question beneath all of it:

How do we participate in the world without being shaped by everything it worships?
For generations, Christians have wrestled with this tension. Some retreat from culture, afraid of what it might do to their faith. Others assimilate so completely that their faith has little to say about how they work, create, lead, or imagine a different future.
One response is separatism. Another is syncretism.

But what if there is another way?
In Jeremiah 29, God tells His people to seek the flourishing of Babylon without becoming Babylon. In Daniel 3, three young men serve within the empire but refuse to bow when it demands their allegiance.
They were present without being absorbed. Faithful without withdrawing. Formed by God, yet committed to the flourishing of the world around them.

This is the vision of a creative minority.
The Creative Edge is a monthly gathering hosted by Axis, bringing together artists, entrepreneurs, designers, educators, founders, and others working at the intersection of faith and culture.
Together, we'll explore theology, formation, creativity, culture, and vocation and ask how following Jesus changes the way we imagine, build, lead, and create.

For our inaugural edition, we're delighted to welcome Lanaire Aderemi as our guest contributor.

MEET OUR GUEST CONTRIBUTOR: dr. lanaire aderemi
Dr. Lanaire Aderemi is an award-winning creative practitioner, writer, and founder of LAP, a creative agency and production company committed to amplifying and archiving untold stories.
With a PhD in Creative Writing and a multidisciplinary practice spanning theatre, film, and audio, her work brings together storytelling, cultural memory, and the lives and histories too often left unheard.
Having worked with organisations including the BBC, British Council, Tate Modern, and V&A Museum, Lanaire brings a rich perspective on the power of stories to shape how we see ourselves, our culture, and the world around us.

Together, we'll make room for the questions that matter: What shapes our creative imagination? How does our faith inform the stories we tell, the work we produce, and the cultures we help create? And what might it look like to practise our craft with both spiritual depth and cultural responsibility?

This isn't about escaping the world or simply fitting into it. It's about becoming the kind of people who can participate in shaping it without losing sight of the One who has called us to be here.
Because the future is being imagined right now. And the things we create, the cultures we shape, and the lives we lead will tell a story about what we believe.

Who is forming your imagination? And what kind of world is it teaching you to create?
Come be part of the conversation.
THE CREATIVE EDGE
Forming a creative minority.
Hosted by Axis.
The Future Belongs to Formed People.

Two days. Two energies. One shared experience.

events.description:
NIGERIA’S DIGITAL FUTURE RUNS ON TRUST AND WE CONVERGE TO DEFINE HOW IT STAYS SECURE.
Nigeria's economy is becoming increasingly digital, but the rapid expansion of digital services has created a parallel challenge: trust. Consumers are navigating an ecosystem of banks, fintechs, telecommunications companies, e‑commerce platforms, marketplaces, insurers, government services and technology providers, all of which increasingly depend on digital identity, data and connected systems. As these systems become more interconnected, the consequences of a security breach can extend far beyond a single organisation.

The CyberTrust Leaders Roundtable is a new executive platform designed to bring together the leaders responsible for cybersecurity, risk, fraud prevention, trust and safety, compliance, data protection and digital transformation across Nigeria's most digitally connected industries. The event will convene C‑level executives, cybersecurity leaders, regulators, policymakers and technology providers across financial services, telecommunications, e‑commerce, technology, insurance, government and other critical sectors to examine how businesses can protect their systems, customers and data in an increasingly complex threat environment. The conversations will examine how organisations can build more resilient digital systems, protect customers and businesses, strengthen identity and authentication, share intelligence and respond to emerging threats.

From cyber‑enabled fraud and identity theft to AI‑powered attacks, deepfakes, data breaches and digital identity, the CyberTrust Leaders Roundtable focuses on the threats that can undermine confidence in digital services and the technologies, policies and partnerships required to build more resilient organisations.

events.description:
You have an idea. Or a skill you’ve spent months learning. Now comes the question: what do you build with it?

That’s where we’re starting with Pre-TechForge 2026.
Before the main event, we’re bringing people together online to talk about the work: getting an idea off the ground, finding your place in tech, and building something people actually need.

And that conversation doesn’t end online. It continues in person at TechForge 2026, where we bring the builders, ideas and questions into one room for a full day of learning, connection and building.

TechForge 2026

The Builders’ Blueprint: Skills, Strategy and Innovation for the Future

600+ builders. 10+ speakers. One room. One full day.

On December 5, developers, designers, founders, product people, tech professionals and emerging talent come together in Lagos for a full day built around becoming better at what they do — and clearer about where they’re going next.

TechForge 2026 isn't another “inspiration-only” tech event.

We're bringing together people who have built, led, invested, experimented, failed, learned and figured things out — for practical conversations about what it actually takes to build a career, a product and a future in technology.

The Builders’ Blueprint is built around three things:

Skills: Practical knowledge you can take away and apply.

Strategy: How to think, position yourself, make better decisions and turn what you know into progress.

Innovation: What's changing with AI and emerging technology, what it means for you, and how to build for what's coming.

Who is TechForge for?

Builders. Developers. Designers. Product people. Founders. Students. Tech professionals. And people still figuring out where they belong in the ecosystem.

Whether you're already building or trying to find your path into tech, the goal is the same: leave with more clarity, better connections and something you can actually use.

What should you expect?

Talks, practical sessions, honest panel conversations, Q&A and intentional networking — all in a single-stage experience.

No choosing between five rooms. No wondering if you're missing the better session somewhere else.

We're putting 600+ people in one room, learning together, asking the hard questions, meeting people they otherwise might never meet, and building the same momentum.

Come curious. Leave with a blueprint.

TechForge 2026 is organized by Infinite Community.
